description: Pre-written maternal library keyed by gestational week and weekday.
disclaimer: General health education only. Not a substitute for professional care.

serving_rules.compute_week: From EDD: clamp(40 - days_until_edd/7, 1, 42). From LMP: weeks since LMP.
serving_rules.daily_select: week_start<=user_week<=week_end AND (weekday is null OR weekday=today); one card per slot.

items.title: Early days — rest and confirmation
items.body: You may only have a positive test or very early symptoms. Focus on rest, hydration, and booking your first antenatal contact when you can. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Folic acid matters early
items.body: If your clinician advised folic acid, take it as prescribed. Leafy greens and fortified foods support early development. Avoid alcohol. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Heavy bleeding or severe pain
items.body: Soaking pads quickly, passing clots, or severe one-sided pain needs urgent care — these can signal miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.
items.cta_label: SOS if bleeding or severe pain

items.title: Save your callback number
items.body: In Profile, confirm the phone dispatchers and drivers should call. Keep Medical ID (blood group if known) up to date.

items.title: It is okay to feel uncertain
items.body: Early pregnancy brings hope and anxiety. Share concerns with a trusted person. Solace is here if a medical emergency arises.

items.title: Nausea and fatigue are common
items.body: Small frequent meals, ginger tea if tolerated, and short rests can help. Persistent vomiting that stops you keeping fluids down needs clinical review. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Protein and steady energy
items.body: Try eggs, beans, yoghurt, or soft meats if you can keep them down. Sip water through the day even if food is hard.

items.title: Smell and taste changes
items.body: Strong smells may trigger nausea. Bland foods (rice, plantain, bread) often sit better.

items.title: One-sided pain or shoulder tip pain
items.body: Severe pain on one side of the abdomen, dizziness, or fainting can be an emergency. Do not wait it out alone. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Antenatal booking
items.body: Plan your first clinic visit. Note allergies and medications in Medical ID for responders.

items.title: Tell one support person
items.body: Choose who you will call day or night. Add their number in your emergency profile when possible.

items.title: End of the first trimester approaches
items.body: Energy may slowly return for some people. Continue prenatal vitamins as advised. Report any bleeding to your clinician. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Iron-rich meals
items.body: Beans, lean meat, leafy vegetables, and fortified cereals help. Pair plant iron with citrus or tomatoes when you can.

items.title: Constipation and bloating
items.body: Water, walking, and fibre (fruit, vegetables, oats) help. Ask your clinician before any laxative.

items.title: Bleeding with pain or dizziness
items.body: Any bright red bleeding with cramps, weakness, or fainting is an emergency — use Solace SOS or go to care immediately. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Know your nearest capable facility
items.body: Ask your clinician which hospital is appropriate for obstetric emergencies near you.

items.title: Mood swings are common
items.body: Hormones and fatigue affect mood. Persistent hopelessness deserves professional support.

items.title: Second trimester — often a steadier phase
items.body: Many people feel more energy. Keep antenatal appointments and ask about vaccines your clinic recommends. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Calcium patterns
items.body: Dairy, fortified alternatives, and local clinical advice on supplements support bone health.

items.title: Round ligament twinges
items.body: Sharp side pulls when standing quickly are common. Severe or constant pain still needs checking. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Fever, chills, or burning urine
items.body: High fever or inability to keep fluids needs timely care in pregnancy. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Document blood group if known
items.body: If you know your blood group, save it under Medical ID.

items.title: Share the plan with family
items.body: Explain that Solace can request an ambulance if something feels wrong.

items.title: Movement and checks
items.body: You may feel flutters. Attend scheduled checks your clinic offers. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Balanced plates
items.body: Protein, vegetable or fruit, and a staple most meals. Limit sugary drinks.

items.title: Back support
items.body: Soft shoes and a pillow behind your back when sitting reduce strain.

items.title: Severe headache or vision changes
items.body: Sudden severe headache, vision spots, or sudden facial swelling need urgent care. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Birth preference notes
items.body: Note preferred hospital and allergies in Profile.

items.title: Mid-pregnancy check-in
items.body: Confirm visit dates, medication list, and callback number.

items.title: Growing belly — posture and rest
items.body: Short walks and side-lying rest often help. Report rhythmic painful tightenings before 37 weeks. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Hydration target
items.body: Regular water intake (about 2–3 litres unless restricted). Dehydration can worsen tightenings.

items.title: Leg cramps at night
items.body: Gentle calf stretches and fluids help some. Sudden one-sided leg swelling with pain needs urgent review. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Fluid leak or gush
items.body: Continuous watery leak may be ruptured membranes. Note time and colour; seek care. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Hospital bag draft list
items.body: ID, clinic card, pads, clean clothes, phone charger, transport plan for support person.

items.title: Sleep disruption
items.body: Side-lying with a pillow between knees helps many.

items.title: Third trimester approaching
items.body: Baby movements become a daily language. Learn what is normal for you. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Iron and vitamin C
items.body: If prescribed iron, take as directed — often with vitamin C rich food.

items.title: Heartburn
items.body: Smaller meals; avoid lying flat right after eating. Ask before antacids.

items.title: Reduced movements
items.body: If movements are clearly less than usual, contact maternity care or use Solace SOS. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Who comes with you
items.body: Agree which person meets you at hospital and handles other logistics.

items.title: Anxiety about birth
items.body: Write questions for your next clinic visit. Emergency planning with Solace is one practical step.

items.title: Week 28 — stay tuned to movements
items.body: At week 28, keep a simple sense of your baby daily pattern. Report a clear drop the same day. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Steady meals, less long fasting
items.body: Long gaps without food can make you dizzy. Carry a small snack when you leave home.

items.title: Swelling watch
items.body: Mild ankle swelling after standing is common. Sudden face or hand swelling with headache is not. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Pre-eclampsia warning pattern
items.body: Severe headache, vision sparks, upper abdominal pain, or sudden swelling need urgent review or SOS. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Confirm Solace Medical ID
items.body: Verify name, phone, blood group, and Maternal care plan in Profile.

items.title: Rest without guilt
items.body: Naps and saying no to extra tasks protect you and the baby.

items.title: Kick awareness (guidance only)
items.body: Know your baby pattern; act the same day if it changes markedly. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Week 32 — birth preparation mode
items.body: Week 32: keep phone charged and bag ready. Painful regular contractions need assessment. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Small frequent meals
items.body: Smaller portions may reduce heartburn.

items.title: Side sleeping
items.body: Left-side lying is often encouraged. Use pillows for belly and knees. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Vaginal bleeding after 28 weeks
items.body: Any fresh bleeding in late pregnancy is an emergency until proven otherwise. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Water broke (PROM)
items.body: A gush or steady trickle of fluid: note time and colour. Seek maternity care. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Hospital bag essentials
items.body: Clinic notes, ID, pads, outfits, charger, snacks for support person.

items.title: Week 37 — term pregnancy
items.body: At week 37 keep bag ready and day/night transport plans. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Easy-to-digest energy
items.body: Light meals you tolerate. Stay hydrated unless told otherwise.

items.title: Pelvic pressure
items.body: Heaviness is common. Cannot pass urine, or pain with fever, needs review. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: You can ask for help early
items.body: If something feels wrong, early contact is better than delay. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Labour signs vs emergency
items.body: Waters breaking, fresh bleeding, severe headache, or movements stopping — use SOS when needed. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Past your due date
items.body: Many births occur after the estimated date. Report reduced movements immediately. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Do not ignore movement changes
items.body: At post-term, same-day assessment for reduced movements is critical. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Know induction discussion points
items.body: Your clinic may discuss induction. Keep Solace ready for unplanned labour at home. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Patience and vigilance together
items.body: Rest when you can, but stay alert to danger signs. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Severe persistent headache & vision
items.body: Severe headache with blurred vision or spots needs urgent obstetric assessment. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Marked reduction in fetal movements
items.body: Fewer movements than your normal pattern — same-day review or SOS. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Regular painful contractions
items.body: Painful tightenings that grow longer and closer — especially with fluid leak or bleeding — warrant urgent care. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: After birth — first days (read when relevant)
items.body: Heavy soaking of pads hourly, large clots, fever, severe headache, or difficulty breathing need urgent care. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Post-birth bleeding emergency
items.body: Soaking more than one pad per hour for more than two hours, or feeling faint with bleeding, is an emergency. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.

items.title: Keep GPS and phone ready
items.body: Allow location permission and keep a charged power bank if outages are common.

items.title: Solace is for emergencies and urgent transport
items.body: Daily tips support awareness. Sudden severe symptoms belong on the SOS path. This is general guidance, not a diagnosis. If you feel unsafe or unsure, use Solace SOS or seek care now.
